patient.label: Patient
patient.definition: A person represented in EMBED and associated with clinical imaging, report, risk, procedure, or pathology records.
caveats: The catalog does not establish complete longitudinal care or outside-system follow-up.

breast_imaging_episode.label: Breast-imaging episode
breast_imaging_episode.definition: A clinically related set of one or more breast-imaging exams, potentially represented through same-episode accession links.
caveats: Episode identity and boundaries can remain incomplete when a representation relies on optional links among exams.

imaging_exam.label: Breast-imaging exam
imaging_exam.definition: A breast-imaging study or accession at exam grain.
caveats: An exam row does not by itself establish a screening, diagnostic, or follow-up cohort role.
Linked exams may be part of the same episode without being earlier or later follow-up.

breast_side.label: Breast side
breast_side.definition: A left- or right-breast view of an exam used for laterality-specific findings and aggregates.
breast_side.grain: one breast side within an exam
caveats: A null side on a finding can represent bilateral involvement, while null procedure side generally means unknown.
The semantic object must not inherit one catalog-wide null-laterality rule.

imaging_finding.label: Imaging finding
imaging_finding.definition: A radiologist-recorded breast-imaging observation with modality-specific descriptors and optional later clinical attribution.
caveats: Finding numbers are not globally unique and include a documented synthetic sentinel.
A finding is not equivalent to a later procedure or pathology diagnosis.

imaging_interpretation.label: Imaging interpretation
imaging_interpretation.definition: The assessment and recommendation associated with an imaging finding.
caveats: Assessment and recommendation are separate fields and must not be collapsed into pathology truth.

procedure.label: Linked breast procedure
procedure.definition: A biopsy, surgery, or other tissue-related procedure represented with procedure-associated pathology information.
caveats: A procedure-to-finding association may be absent or ambiguous.

pathology_observation.label: Pathology observation
pathology_observation.definition: A procedure-associated pathology descriptor observation recorded in one of the pathology code slots.
caveats: Slot position and duplicate occurrence are not informative for clinical decision-making.
Some valid source-system codes have unresolved meanings.

pathology_diagnosis.label: Pathology diagnosis state
pathology_diagnosis.definition: The represented diagnostic severity group derived from attached procedure-associated pathology descriptors.
caveats: The six coded states exclude the separate state in which no pathology is attached.
A represented diagnosis does not establish complete outcome capture or follow-up.

radiology_report.label: Radiology report
radiology_report.definition: A versioned radiology report associated with an imaging accession.
caveats: Report text may contain sensitive content and is not exposed by this tool.

risk_assessment.label: Breast-cancer risk assessment
risk_assessment.definition: A represented set of named clinical risk-model outputs associated with a patient and optionally an exam.
caveats: Risk-output interpretation depends on the named model, version, units, and field-specific exceptional-value semantics.
A risk output is not an imaging assessment or pathology diagnosis.

breast_side.architectural_distortion_agg.label: Side-level architectural distortion aggregate
breast_side.architectural_distortion_agg.definition: Breast-side-level Boolean summary of mammography finding-level architectural-distortion presence.
caveats: This summary is aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT; it does not summarize non-mammography modalities.

breast_side.asymmetry_aggregate.label: Side-level asymmetry aggregate
breast_side.asymmetry_aggregate.definition: Breast-side-level Boolean summary of mammography finding-level asymmetry presence.
caveats: This summary is aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT; it does not summarize non-mammography modalities.

breast_side.calcification_aggregate.label: Side-level calcification aggregate
breast_side.calcification_aggregate.definition: Breast-side-level Boolean summary of mammography finding-level calcification presence.
caveats: This summary is aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT; it does not summarize non-mammography modalities.

breast_side.mass_aggregate.label: Side-level mass aggregate
breast_side.mass_aggregate.definition: Breast-side-level Boolean summary of mammography finding-level mass presence.
caveats: This summary is aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT; it does not summarize non-mammography modalities.

breast_side.pathology_severity_aggregate.label: Side-level pathology severity aggregate
breast_side.pathology_severity_aggregate.definition: Minimum, and therefore most severe, pathology-severity value among procedure-associated pathology records in the breast-side aggregate group.
caveats: Pathology severity uses inverse ordering, so the minimum value is the most severe.

missing_states.meaning: No pathology severity is attached within the represented breast-side aggregate group; this is not a diagnosis category or negative outcome.
caveats: It does not establish benign disease, no cancer, complete capture, or adequate follow-up for the breast side.

breast.side.label: Breast side
caveats: For a side attached to a clinical finding, null represents a bilateral finding.
Outside the finding-side context, null generally represents unknown laterality; in particular, a null biopsy or procedure side must not be interpreted as bilateral.

demographics.age_at_exam.label: Anonymized age at exam
demographics.age_at_exam.definition: Age in years at the exam, calculated from the consistently shifted patient birth date and study date.

demographics.age_at_menopause.label: Anonymized menopause age

demographics.age_at_pregnancy.label: Anonymized pregnancy age

exam.architectural_distortion_aggregate.label: Exam-level architectural distortion aggregate

exam.calcification_aggregate.label: Exam-level calcification aggregate

exam.left_finding_total.definition: Count of distinct findings recorded on the left breast during the exam.

exam.location.label: Anonymized exam location
caveats: The mapping to the legend's unsuffixed loc_num header is inferred, and the listed sites are not guaranteed exhaustive.

exam.mammography_type.label: Mammography exam type
exam.mammography_type.definition: Exam type derived from the exam description.
caveats: Null semantics are not documented and must not be inferred from the code meanings.

exam.mass_aggregate.label: Exam-level mass aggregate
exam.mass_aggregate.definition: Exam-level Boolean summary of mammography finding-level mass presence.
caveats: This summary is aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT; it does not summarize non-mammography modalities.

exam.modality.label: Imaging modality
caveats: Null semantics are not documented and must not be inferred from the code meanings.

exam.pathology_severity_aggregate.label: Exam-level pathology severity aggregate
exam.pathology_severity_aggregate.definition: Minimum, and therefore most severe, pathology-severity value among procedure-associated pathology records in the exam aggregate group.
caveats: Pathology severity uses inverse ordering, so the minimum value is the most severe.

missing_states.meaning: No pathology severity is attached within the represented exam aggregate group; this is not a diagnosis category or negative outcome.

exam.procedure_description.label: Procedure description

exam.procedure_related_flag.label: Procedure-related exam flag

exam.release_version.label: EMBED data version

exam.right_finding_total.label: Right finding total

exam.study_date.label: Anonymized exam date

exam.visit_type.label: Visit type

imaging.depth.label: Imaging finding depth

imaging.distance.label: Imaging finding distance
caveats: Negative and zero values require an explicit sentinel policy.

imaging.finding_number.label: Finding number
imaging.finding_number.definition: Finding identifier within an accession, except for reserved synthetic entries.
caveats: The reserved value -9 identifies a derived synthetic contralateral negative finding implied by a non-negative finding on the other breast but not explicitly entered in MagView.
Synthetic contralateral negatives are derived records rather than manually entered findings.
After excluding the reserved -9 synthetic records, (acc_anon, numfind) identifies a distinct clinical finding within an accession; side is not part of that clinical identity.
One clinical finding can occupy multiple physical rows because of attached procedures or later table construction and merges.
The tuple is not a persistent lesion identifier across accessions, episodes, or modalities.

imaging.finding_size.label: Imaging finding size
caveats: Negative and zero values require an explicit sentinel policy.

imaging.linked_accession_identifier.label: Linked exam accession identifier
imaging.linked_accession_identifier.definition: Anonymized accession reference for a same-episode exam linked at study time.
caveats: Treat identifiers as opaque; do not expose values or assume stability beyond the documented release.
A non-null reference is expected to identify a same-episode exam, but release and data-quality edge cases may not resolve to the exported exam table.
The reference does not identify a prior or follow-up exam; compare study dates when temporal context is needed.

imaging.linked_study_flag.label: Linked study flag
caveats: The flag is expected to identify a linked same-episode exam, but data-quality edge cases mean it must not be used to repair a missing linked-accession value.

clinical.patient-imaging-episode.label: Patient has breast-imaging episode
clinical.patient-imaging-episode.attribution: Clinical ownership of an episode by a patient.
attribution_limitations: A profile may represent episode membership through incomplete exam links rather than a canonical episode identifier.
clinical.patient-imaging-episode.temporal_qualification: Episodes occur during the patient's represented timeline; no completeness is implied.
caveats: A patient with no represented episode must not be interpreted as having no breast-imaging care.

clinical.episode-exam.label: Episode contains imaging exam
clinical.episode-exam.attribution: Clinical grouping of exams into a breast-imaging episode.
attribution_limitations: Profile bindings based on same-episode links can be optional and incomplete.
Unlinked exams may still be clinically related.
clinical.episode-exam.temporal_qualification: Linked accessions identify same-episode exams, not prior or follow-up direction.
caveats: No deterministic episode-construction algorithm is supplied.

clinical.patient-exam.label: Patient has imaging exam
clinical.patient-exam.attribution: Patient ownership of each imaging accession, supporting traversal across all represented exams in that patient's timeline.
attribution_limitations: Release-local identifiers and incomplete longitudinal capture limit portability.

A task may retain exam-side or finding output grain, but searches for prior, subsequent, nearest, or interval events must first consider candidate exams across the patient timeline rather than only the index accession.
clinical.patient-exam.temporal_qualification: Each exam has its own event date within a patient timeline; same-day inclusion, episode membership, and tie-breaking remain declared analyst choices.
caveats: This direct relation does not replace the clinically useful episode layer.
Do not equate a candidate event's accession with an index accession merely because the final result is reported at exam-side or finding grain.

clinical.exam-side.label: Exam includes breast side
clinical.exam-side.attribution: Laterality-specific component of a breast-imaging exam.
attribution_limitations: Unilateral and bilateral exams create different numbers of represented sides.
clinical.exam-side.temporal_qualification: The side is part of the same exam event.
caveats: Finding laterality and procedure laterality have different null semantics.

clinical.exam-finding.label: Exam records imaging finding
clinical.exam-finding.attribution: An imaging finding is recorded for an exam accession.
attribution_limitations: Synthetic negative findings and non-unique tuples complicate row identity.
clinical.exam-finding.temporal_qualification: The finding is documented in the exam context.
caveats: Absence of a finding row is not a universal negative interpretation.

clinical.side-finding.label: Breast side relates to imaging finding
clinical.side-finding.attribution: Laterality attribution of an imaging finding.
attribution_limitations: Bilateral findings can be represented with null finding side rather than two side links.
clinical.side-finding.temporal_qualification: The relation is part of the exam interpretation, not a later procedure attribution.
caveats: Null laterality must be interpreted by field role.

clinical.finding-interpretation.label: Finding has imaging interpretation
clinical.finding-interpretation.attribution: Finding-level association of assessment and recommendation.
attribution_limitations: A profile may co-locate the interpretation with a finding rather than identify it independently.
clinical.finding-interpretation.temporal_qualification: No separate interpretation timestamp is represented.
caveats: An assessment category is not tissue diagnosis truth.

clinical.interpretation-procedure.label: Interpretation may lead to procedure
clinical.interpretation-procedure.attribution: Clinical association between an interpretation or recommendation and a later procedure.
attribution_limitations: A recommendation does not prove a procedure occurred.
A profile may lack a complete direct recommendation-to-procedure key.
clinical.interpretation-procedure.temporal_qualification: The procedure generally occurs after the imaging interpretation, but no universal interval is defined.
caveats: This relationship describes clinical adjacency rather than an executable linkage.

clinical.finding-procedure.label: Finding may be attributed to procedure
clinical.finding-procedure.attribution: Manual or source-system attribution of a later procedure to an imaging finding.
attribution_limitations: Attribution can be missing, duplicated, or many-to-many.
A diagnostic-study procedure may not be back-attributed to an earlier screening finding.
clinical.finding-procedure.temporal_qualification: The procedure is downstream of the original finding; the represented exam link does not define a universal time window.
caveats: No deterministic repair or backfill rule is supplied.

clinical.procedure-pathology-observation.label: Procedure produces pathology observation
clinical.procedure-pathology-observation.attribution: Procedure-associated tissue observation recorded in a pathology descriptor slot.
attribution_limitations: Procedure and pathology fields share a physical row but do not have separately proven identities.
clinical.procedure-pathology-observation.temporal_qualification: Pathology observation is downstream of tissue sampling or surgery.
caveats: Row co-location must not be promoted to one-to-one clinical cardinality.

clinical.pathology-observation-diagnosis.label: Pathology observations support diagnosis state
clinical.pathology-observation-diagnosis.attribution: Classification of attached pathology descriptors into the most severe represented diagnosis group.
attribution_limitations: Unknown descriptor meanings may limit interpretation.
Duplicate slots do not create additional diagnostic weight.
clinical.pathology-observation-diagnosis.temporal_qualification: The diagnosis is documented after the associated observation; exact availability is not established.
caveats: The inverse severity scale is an implementation value ordering, not disease chronology.

clinical.patient-pathology-observation.label: Patient has represented pathology observation
clinical.patient-pathology-observation.attribution: Patient attribution inherited by traversing from each candidate pathology observation's associated accession to that candidate exam and then to its patient.
attribution_limitations: A profile may carry patient attribution indirectly through an exam or accession relationship.
The pathology row's accession identifies its own associated candidate exam; it is not necessarily the index exam accession used by a longitudinal analysis.
The pathology-to-exam association alone does not implement patient-level longitudinal ascertainment; the candidate exam must also be attributed to the patient.
clinical.patient-pathology-observation.temporal_qualification: The observation occurs within the patient's represented clinical timeline and can be compared with qualifying index exams only after patient attribution; same-day inclusion and nearest-event tie-breaking remain analyst choices.
caveats: This semantic relation requires the two-edge open-v2 traversal pathology accession to candidate exam to patient; no single pathology-to-exam binding is a complete patient-pathology implementation.

clinical.exam-pathology-observation.label: Exam associated with pathology observation
clinical.exam-pathology-observation.attribution: Accession association carried by the pathology representation.
attribution_limitations: The accession relationship is not an enforced foreign key and does not imply contemporaneous availability.
clinical.exam-pathology-observation.temporal_qualification: Pathology may follow the associated imaging exam.
caveats: The associated exam is not automatically a diagnosis-date anchor.

clinical.side-pathology-observation.label: Breast side may be attributed pathology observation
clinical.side-pathology-observation.attribution: Laterality association between a pathology record and breast side.
attribution_limitations: The registered relationship uses finding side rather than biopsy side and may be incomplete.
clinical.side-pathology-observation.temporal_qualification: The pathology observation is downstream of the exam-side finding context.
caveats: Do not substitute procedure-side fields for finding-side linkage.

clinical.finding-pathology-observation.label: Finding may be attributed pathology observation
clinical.finding-pathology-observation.attribution: Represented attribution between imaging finding and pathology record.
attribution_limitations: The accession-side-finding tuple is optional and many-to-many.
Incomplete tuples and duplicate matches require an explicit analysis reconciliation policy.
clinical.finding-pathology-observation.temporal_qualification: Pathology is downstream; attribution does not make it available at imaging time.
caveats: No one-to-one finding truth label is implied.

clinical.exam-report.label: Exam has radiology report version
clinical.exam-report.attribution: Accession association of one or more represented report versions.
attribution_limitations: Duplicate natural tuples and missing links can occur.
clinical.exam-report.temporal_qualification: Report versions document the exam and may evolve after initial interpretation.
caveats: Joining reports to findings by accession can multiply both sides.

clinical.patient-report.label: Patient has radiology report
clinical.patient-report.attribution: Patient reference carried by the report representation.
attribution_limitations: The patient-report tuple is not a proven unique clinical key.
clinical.patient-report.temporal_qualification: Reports occur within the patient's represented imaging timeline.
caveats: Report content is not exposed by this context service.

clinical.patient-risk-assessment.label: Patient has risk assessment
clinical.patient-risk-assessment.attribution: Patient association of a represented risk score set.
attribution_limitations: The natural identity and completeness of risk rows remain limited.
clinical.patient-risk-assessment.temporal_qualification: Risk outputs were calculated during clinical care, but exact availability time is unresolved.
caveats: No risk record is approved for modeling merely because it is represented.

clinical.exam-risk-assessment.label: Exam may have risk assessment

attribution_limitations: Not every exam has a risk record and some risk references may not resolve.
clinical.exam-risk-assessment.temporal_qualification: The assessment was calculated during care; exact within-episode timing is unresolved.

time.specimen-collection.label: Specimen collection time

time.pathology-report-documentation.label: Pathology report documentation time
time.pathology-report-documentation.meaning: The anonymized pathology-report date represents documentation or reporting of pathology information.

Do not coalesce procedure, specimen, report, or imaging-exam dates into one event timestamp.

time.downstream-availability.label: Downstream clinical information availability
time.downstream-availability.meaning: The time by which procedure, pathology observation, or pathology diagnosis information was available for a particular use.
caveats: A selected profile may not provide a field-level availability timestamp; inspect profile coverage.
Co-location in a wide row does not establish contemporaneous availability.

aggregation.pathology-observation-severi.label: Pathology observations to diagnosis severity
aggregation.pathology-observation-severi.method: Select the most severe attached descriptor group across the procedure-associated pathology slots.
aggregation.pathology-observation-severi.ordering: Inverse severity ordering: lower numeric groups are more severe.
caveats: Duplicate descriptor occurrences are equivalent to one occurrence.
Unknown descriptor mappings remain unresolved even when a severity group is represented.

aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side.label: Pathology severity to breast side
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side.method: Take the minimum represented pathology-severity value in the applicable breast-side group.
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side.ordering: Inverse severity ordering: minimum means most severe.
caveats: The physical grouping and attachment limitations still apply.
Null does not become benign during aggregation.

aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam.label: Pathology severity to imaging exam
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam.method: Take the minimum represented pathology-severity value in the applicable exam group.
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam.ordering: Inverse severity ordering: minimum means most severe.
caveats: An exam aggregate does not establish that pathology was available at imaging time.
Null does not establish a negative outcome.

aggregation.pathology-severity-to-findin.label: Pathology severity to imaging finding
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-findin.method: No supplied finding-level severity aggregation is established; an analyst may declare a task-specific policy such as any linked outcome, earliest linked outcome, or minimum linked severity.
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-findin.ordering: The declared policy must address optional many-to-many attribution, row multiplication, time, and estimand dependence.
caveats: Do not silently deduplicate multiplied joins.
The catalog does not select a finding-level outcome policy.
Incomplete linkage and multiplicity remain visible limitations even when a declared policy is reasonable.

aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patien.label: Pathology severity to patient
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patien.method: No supplied patient-level diagnosis aggregation is defined; a task-specific policy must select time, recurrence, multiplicity, and state transitions.
aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patien.ordering: No universal ordering across a patient's episodes is selected beyond the coded severity ordering within represented groups.
caveats: A patient may have multiple sides, exams, procedures, diagnoses, and changing states over time.
The catalog does not define incident, prevalent, earliest, or ever-positive patient outcomes.

guardrail.null-pathology-not-negative.title: Unattached pathology is not a negative diagnosis
guardrail.null-pathology-not-negative.statement: Do not classify null pathology severity or absent attached pathology as benign, no cancer, or adequate negative follow-up.
guardrail.null-pathology-not-negative.rationale: The represented null state means no pathology is attached; it does not establish disease absence or outcome ascertainment.
caveats: A task-specific study may measure follow-up, but the catalog does not supply that policy.

guardrail.assessment-not-pathology.title: Imaging assessment is not pathology truth
guardrail.assessment-not-pathology.statement: Do not substitute an imaging assessment or recommendation for a tissue diagnosis.
guardrail.assessment-not-pathology.rationale: Assessment guides next clinical actions; pathology observations and diagnoses are distinct downstream objects.
caveats: The catalog describes representation and does not prescribe care.

guardrail.downstream-temporal-leakage.title: Downstream clinical information may cause temporal leakage
guardrail.downstream-temporal-leakage.statement: Procedure, pathology, and later report information must not be assumed available at an earlier imaging or prediction time.
guardrail.downstream-temporal-leakage.rationale: Event, documentation, and availability times differ, and wide-row co-location does not prove co-availability.
caveats: The appropriate availability boundary is analysis specific.

guardrail.explicit-attribution-policy.title: Finding-to-pathology attribution requires an explicit policy
guardrail.explicit-attribution-policy.statement: Do not treat finding, procedure, or pathology attribution as one-to-one or silently deduplicate multiplied rows.
guardrail.explicit-attribution-policy.rationale: Represented attribution is optional and many-to-many; incomplete tuples and duplicate matches can change grain and interpretation.
caveats: No automatic matching or reconciliation algorithm is provided.

guardrail.explicit-grain-aggregation.title: Changing clinical grain requires an explicit aggregation policy
guardrail.explicit-grain-aggregation.statement: Moving among finding, side, exam, episode, and patient grain requires a declared aggregation, multiplicity, and time policy.
guardrail.explicit-grain-aggregation.rationale: The same person can have multiple exams, sides, findings, procedures, and diagnoses; supplied aggregates cover only documented transitions.
caveats: The catalog does not select a canonical cohort or patient-level outcome.

guardrail.longitudinal-search-is-patient.title: Longitudinal candidate search is patient-scoped
guardrail.longitudinal-search-is-patient.statement: Search candidate prior or subsequent exams, procedures, and pathology across the represented patient timeline; do not restrict candidate ascertainment to the index accession.
guardrail.longitudinal-search-is-patient.rationale: The output can remain at exam-side or finding grain, but a candidate pathology row's accession identifies its own associated exam. Patient-level traversal requires pathology accession to candidate exam to patient before comparison with qualifying index exams for that patient.
caveats: Incomplete represented follow-up still limits ascertainment after patient-scoped traversal.
This guardrail does not choose same-day boundaries, episode definitions, tie-breaking, or a preferred event timestamp.

guardrail.longitudinal-boundaries-are-an.title: Longitudinal boundaries and tie-breaking require declared choices
guardrail.longitudinal-boundaries-are-an.statement: Declare whether subsequent excludes same-day events, whether separate same-day procedures remain distinct, how episodes are defined, and how equally near candidates are handled.
guardrail.longitudinal-boundaries-are-an.rationale: These choices determine temporal membership and multiplicity but are not representation failures, and the catalog does not select them.
caveats: A study request may itself fix one of these policies; otherwise it should be declared by the analyst.

guardrail.timestamps-answer-different-qu.title: Different clinical timestamps answer different questions
guardrail.timestamps-answer-different-qu.statement: Select exam, procedure, specimen, pathology-report, and availability times by their clinical meaning. Do not coalesce them into a single event timestamp or use one as a fallback for a missing value of another semantic endpoint.
guardrail.timestamps-answer-different-qu.rationale: These timestamps refer to different events or documentation stages. Missingness in the selected temporal semantic remains missing; another semantic may be analyzed as a separately named endpoint or sensitivity analysis, not substituted into the same endpoint.
caveats: Agents and users remain responsible for task-specific anchors and windows.
A cancer-associated imaging exam remains a valid anchor when that is the explicitly named estimand; it is not a replacement for a different clinical event.

guardrail.inverse-severity-ordering.title: Pathology severity uses inverse ordering
guardrail.inverse-severity-ordering.statement: Do not select the numeric maximum as the most severe pathology result.
guardrail.inverse-severity-ordering.rationale: Values 0 through 5 run from invasive breast cancer toward non-breast cancer, and supplied side/exam aggregates use the minimum.
caveats: Null remains an attachment state, not an ordered negative category.

guardrail.risk-probability-readiness.title: Risk outputs require validation before probability metrics
guardrail.risk-probability-readiness.statement: Do not use the represented risk outputs as probability-like predictions for calibration slope, Brier score, or predicted-versus-observed calibration until their scale, units, exceptional values, model version, horizon meaning, and probability semantics are validated.
guardrail.risk-probability-readiness.rationale: Association or ranking studies may be possible with an explicitly qualified score interpretation, but values such as -35, -2, and 100 and the generating model versions remain unresolved in open-v2.
caveats: This constraint does not mark the physical risk fields unsupported.
A separately justified association or ranking analysis must still report the unresolved score interpretation.

guardrail.attached-pathology-selection.title: Attached pathology conditions on represented tissue sampling
guardrail.attached-pathology-selection.statement: Restricting observations to attached pathology defines a tissue-sampled or pathology-observed estimand rather than a neutral outcome-availability filter.
guardrail.attached-pathology-selection.rationale: Tissue sampling occurs downstream of clinical selection and is not performed for every patient, exam, side, or finding, so pathology-observed groups can differ systematically from unsampled groups; such a cohort is not inherently invalid, but its generalizability and causal interpretation require care.
caveats: The catalog identifies the selection mechanism but does not prescribe an inclusion, exclusion, weighting, or causal-analysis policy.
Accurately name conclusions as applying to the represented tissue-sampled or pathology-observed population.

guardrail.non-breast-cancer-not-no-malig.title: Non-breast cancer is not absence of malignancy
guardrail.non-breast-cancer-not-no-malig.statement: The non-breast-cancer pathology-severity state must not be interpreted as benign, healthy, or free of malignancy.
guardrail.non-breast-cancer-not-no-malig.rationale: The state distinguishes a malignancy that is not classified as breast cancer from benign pathology and from the separate unattached-pathology state.
caveats: Whether this state is eligible for any task-specific comparison group is an analysis decision outside the catalog.

guardrail.colocation-not-coavailability.title: Physical co-location does not imply clinical co-availability
guardrail.colocation-not-coavailability.statement: Do not infer that values projected into the same wide row were observed or available at the same clinical time.
guardrail.colocation-not-coavailability.rationale: Denormalization combines fields from different events and documentation stages without establishing their availability boundary.
caveats: The wide table's construction and field-level co-availability remain unresolved.

guardrail.incomplete-outcome-capture.title: No observed diagnosis is not proven disease absence
guardrail.incomplete-outcome-capture.statement: A zero may validly mean no represented biopsy or cancer event under a declared extraction policy, but it must not be interpreted as never biopsied, cancer-free, or complete negative outcome ascertainment.
guardrail.incomplete-outcome-capture.rationale: Represented-event endpoints can be useful when accurately named. Outside-system outcomes, incomplete attribution, release coverage, and follow-up opportunity limit stronger disease-absence or complete-follow-up claims.
caveats: Follow-up windows, censoring, exclusions, and outcomes are analysis policies.
Follow-up opportunity measures may be used as observation proxies when named as proxies rather than proof of complete follow-up.

coverage.open-v2.downstream-availability.subject: time.downstream-availability

coverage.open-v2.outcome-capture.subject: open-v2.pathology-procedure-context
coverage.open-v2.outcome-capture.summary: The available metadata does not establish complete capture of breast-cancer outcomes, outside-system diagnoses, or longitudinal follow-up.

coverage.open-v2.risk-probability-calibr.subject: open-v2.risk-context
coverage.open-v2.risk-probability-calibr.summary: Open-v2 risk fields are physically represented, but their scale, units, exceptional values, model versions, horizon semantics, and readiness for probability-calibration metrics have not been validated.

coverage.open-v2.patient-pathology-aggre.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patient
coverage.open-v2.patient-pathology-aggre.summary: Open-v2 supplies no canonical patient-level pathology severity field or universal longitudinal outcome rollup.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-s.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side
coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-s.summary: Open-v2 supplies a breast-side pathology-severity result concept whose verified rollup takes the minimum represented severity in the applicable side group.
caveats: Support for the rollup does not remove laterality-attribution or unattached-pathology limitations.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-e.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam
coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-e.summary: Open-v2 supplies an exam pathology-severity result concept whose verified rollup takes the minimum represented severity in the applicable exam group.
caveats: Support for the rollup does not establish pathology availability at exam time or complete outcome capture.

coverage.open-v2.finding-pathology-attri.subject: clinical.finding-pathology-observation
coverage.open-v2.finding-pathology-attri.summary: A physical finding-to-pathology tuple is registered, but its attribution is optional, incomplete, and many-to-many.
caveats: Supported linkage metadata is not complete outcome ascertainment.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-code-meanings.subject: pathology.diagnosis_code_slot
coverage.open-v2.pathology-code-meanings.summary: Some valid source-system pathology codes have no mapping in the released legend or a single authoritative cross-system dictionary.

coverage.open-v2.imaging-episode.subject: breast_imaging_episode

clinical.screening-diagnostic-pathway.title: Screening and diagnostic breast-imaging pathway
clinical.screening-diagnostic-pathway.summary: Screening and diagnostic imaging serve different clinical roles, with tissue sampling and pathology entering later when indicated.

claims.statement: Screening mammography evaluates asymptomatic patients for findings that may require additional diagnostic evaluation.
caveats: This clinical role does not identify an EMBED exam row or define a cohort.

claims.statement: A symptomatic presentation may enter diagnostic imaging without a preceding screening examination.
caveats: Absence of a linked screening record does not by itself prove that symptoms were present.

claims.statement: Diagnostic assessment may resolve a finding, support surveillance, or lead to a recommendation for tissue sampling.
caveats: An assessment category is not interchangeable with pathology truth.

claims.statement: Pathology is produced after tissue sampling or surgery and may inform subsequent treatment or imaging.
caveats: The statement supplies no universal timing window or treatment rule.
This context is general clinical background and is not evidence that open-v2 rows form a complete or deterministic event sequence.
No follow-up interval, interval-cancer policy, outcome definition, or modality-inclusion rule is established.

embed.finding-procedure-recording.title: Public EMBED finding and procedure recording
embed.finding-procedure-recording.summary: Public EMBED documentation distinguishes radiologist-recorded findings from later procedure and pathology information in the classic clinical table.

claims.statement: The public classic-table documentation describes findings as radiologist-recorded observations and procedures as later events linked to a finding.
caveats: This statement does not assert that open-v2 stores both entities in one row.

claims.statement: In the documented classic representation, more than one linked procedure can repeat a finding while procedure details differ.
caveats: Finding-row deduplication must not be transferred to open-v2 without profile-specific evidence.

claims.statement: Public EMBED documentation describes pathology as manually entered after a procedure and attributed back to the originating finding.
caveats: Manual attribution can be incomplete and is not a foreign-key guarantee.

claims.statement: The public documentation warns that pathology may be recorded on a diagnostic study without corresponding attribution to an earlier screening study.
caveats: No frequency, temporal window, or deterministic repair rule is established.
This is EMBED-specific public background, but its classic two-table row layout is not authoritative for open-v2.
The context records provenance and hazards, not a pathology backfill algorithm.

open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.title: Open-v2 assessment and recommendation context
open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.summary: Assessment and recommendation are distinct finding-level fields whose clinical and temporal roles must not be collapsed.

claims.statement: Open-v2 represents imaging assessment and imaging recommendation as separate columns at imaging-finding grain.
caveats: Physical co-location does not make the fields semantically interchangeable.

claims.statement: The released assessment codes identify distinct BI-RADS states and must not be reduced to one simple ordinal scale.
caveats: Code membership alone does not establish workflow validity for a particular exam type.

claims.statement: Recommendation strings come from a loose multi-site MagView reporting schema with expected formatting heterogeneity.
caveats: Preserve the source string rather than imposing a canonical grammar.

claims.statement: Mappings for valid recommendation codes absent from the released legend are currently unknown; there is no single authoritative owner or versioned dictionary across the contributing clinical systems.
caveats: Resolving a code requires system-specific investigation and data processing; do not guess or silently normalize undocumented recommendation codes.

claims.statement: The assessment and recommendation columns in combined_anon are convenience projections, not proof of value equality or contemporaneous availability.
caveats: Use the canonical imaging-finding binding when feature provenance matters.
Do not derive an outcome label from assessment or recommendation without a declared task and temporal anchor.
Public pathway guidance does not establish that open-v2 rows form a complete screening-to-diagnostic sequence.

open-v2.demographic-administrative-conte.title: Open-v2 demographic and administrative semantics
open-v2.demographic-administrative-conte.summary: Open-v2 age, ancestry, legal-sex, and release-version fields retain source-specific definitions and deidentification caveats.

claims.statement: The age-at-exam, menarche-age, menopause-age, and pregnancy-age fields are measured in years; values such as zero are data-quality errors rather than documented sentinel codes.
caveats: The specific pregnancy event represented by pregnancy age remains unresolved.

claims.statement: Age at exam is calculated from the patient birth date and study date after both dates receive the same within-patient shift; it is otherwise unchanged except that ages greater than or equal to 90 are top-coded to 89.
caveats: The shifted calendar dates must not be interpreted literally.

claims.statement: The Ashkenazi indicator represents self-identified Ashkenazi Jewish heritage recorded as a known breast-cancer risk factor.
caveats: Completeness, reliability, encoding, and null semantics are not established.

claims.statement: The released gender-description field represents patient legal sex at the time of the exam.
caveats: This field does not represent gender identity.

claims.statement: The EMBED data-version field records the first EMBED release version in which the element was included.
caveats: It is not a per-row processing-lineage or schema-version guarantee.
Do not convert data-quality errors into sentinel meanings without field-specific evidence.
Administrative legal sex, gender identity, and self-identified heritage are distinct constructs.

open-v2.linked-exam-context.title: Open-v2 linked-exam references
open-v2.linked-exam-context.summary: Linked accession fields identify same-episode exams linked at study time, with expected data-quality and release-coverage edge cases.

claims.statement: A linked accession is an optional reference and is not guaranteed to resolve to an open-v2 exam row.
caveats: Treat accession identifiers as opaque and release-scoped.

claims.statement: Multiple imaging-finding or wide rows may reference the same linked exam, so joined exam attributes can repeat at the source grain.
caveats: This is a row-multiplication hazard, not an empirical frequency claim.

claims.statement: The linked-study flag and linked-accession presence are expected to describe the same same-episode linkage, but data-quality edge cases can violate row-wise equivalence.
caveats: Do not use one field as a missing-value repair for the other.

claims.statement: A linked accession identifies a same-episode exam linked at study time; it does not designate a prior or follow-up exam.
caveats: Use the linked exams' study dates for their temporal context.
Linked references describe relationship metadata and are not executable joins.
Release filtering and ordinary data-quality artifacts can leave expected link or flag invariants unsatisfied in edge cases.

open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.title: Open-v2 multimodal finding context
open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.summary: The imaging-finding surface contains mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor families without proving modality presence from descriptor nulls.

claims.statement: Open-v2 imaging_findings_anon exposes distinct mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor columns.
caveats: A shared table surface does not make modality-specific descriptors interchangeable.

claims.statement: Exam modality is represented separately at exam grain and should remain distinct from individual descriptor fields.
caveats: Cross-field modality consistency has not been registered as a validated invariant.

claims.statement: Modality-specific descriptor fields indicate presence or absence of particular finding descriptors and do not establish whether that modality was performed or available.
caveats: Use the separate exam/modality features for modality availability.

claims.statement: Exam-level and breast-side-level mass, calcification, asymmetry, and architectural-distortion fields are Boolean summaries aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT.
caveats: These summaries do not aggregate ultrasound or MRI descriptors.

claims.statement: After excluding finding number -9, accession and finding number identify a distinct clinical finding within an accession; -9 identifies a derived synthetic contralateral negative finding implied by a non-negative finding on the other breast but not explicitly entered in MagView.
caveats: Synthetic contralateral negatives are derived records.
The clinical identity can occupy multiple physical rows and is not a persistent lesion identifier across accessions, episodes, or modalities.

claims.statement: A null side attached to a clinical finding represents a bilateral finding; outside that context, null generally means unknown laterality and a null biopsy or procedure side is not bilateral.
caveats: Interpret null laterality according to the field's clinical role rather than applying a catalog-wide null rule.

claims.statement: Loosely structured coded fields do not share one guaranteed delimiter, ordering, repetition, composition, or null convention.
caveats: Without field-specific evidence, preserve source strings, treat ordering as non-informative, and treat null as unknown or missing.
Descriptor presence and modality availability are separate questions represented by different features.

open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.title: Open-v2 pathology and procedure context
open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.summary: Pathology findings carry procedure, report, surgery, diagnosis-slot, and severity fields with non-unique links back to imaging.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores pathology findings in a separate pathology-finding-grain table with procedure, report, surgery, and diagnosis fields.
caveats: The table grain does not establish a unique clinical row identity.

claims.statement: The registered pathology-to-imaging association uses accession, finding side, and finding number, but is optional and can match multiple rows in either direction.
caveats: Joining can multiply rows and incomplete tuples require an explicit policy.

claims.statement: The side component of the registered imaging relationship is finding side, not biopsy side.
caveats: Do not substitute bside when following the declared table relationship.

claims.statement: Path1 through path10 are procedure-associated pathology descriptor codes, generally ordered by severity group; slot position, within-group order, and duplicate occurrences are not informative for decision-making.
caveats: Duplicate codes are not intended but may occur and are equivalent to one occurrence.

claims.statement: Pathology descriptor codes observed in open-v2 but absent from the released legend are valid source-system codes with mappings that are currently unknown; there is no single authoritative owner or versioned dictionary across the contributing clinical systems.
caveats: Retain unknown codes as observed; resolving one requires system-specific investigation and data processing.

claims.statement: Pathology severity is the inverse coded group of the most severe attached pathology descriptor: 0 invasive cancer, 1 in-situ cancer, 2 high-risk lesion, 3 borderline lesion, 4 benign finding, and 5 non-breast cancer.
caveats: Lower values are more severe; null means no attached pathology and is not benign or negative.

claims.statement: Exam-level and breast-side-level pathology severity are aggregated by taking the minimum, and therefore most severe, value among procedure-associated pathology records in the applicable group.
caveats: The inverse ordering means an ordinary numeric maximum would select the least severe value.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 bindings expose pathology-severity values and side- and exam-level rollups but no patient-level pathology-severity result field or supplied longitudinal outcome rollup.
caveats: Absence of a supplied field does not prohibit an analyst-defined policy; it means the catalog does not designate one.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 metadata and public pathology-attribution documentation do not establish complete capture of breast-cancer outcomes, outside-system diagnoses, or longitudinal follow-up.
caveats: This is a limitation of available evidence, not a measured estimate of missing outcomes or follow-up.
Procedure and pathology information may postdate imaging and must not be treated as contemporaneous by default.
In the classic MagView representation, distinct procedures carry distinct procedure/pathology values even when the associated finding content is otherwise duplicated.

open-v2.report-context.title: Open-v2 report lifecycle context
open-v2.report-context.summary: Reports are accession-linked records whose sequence orders successive MagView report versions; source heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples and the addendum-flag relationship remains unverified.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores anonymized accession-linked radiology report text with the associated imaging-exam study date and MagView report-version sequence.
caveats: Report content was not read while authoring the catalog.

claims.statement: No tested natural tuple uniquely identifies every report row in the registered open-v2 review.
caveats: The technical export index is not a documented durable report identifier.

claims.statement: MagView increments rseq when a new report version is created; within an accession the minimum represented sequence is earliest and the maximum is latest.
caveats: The specific origin of rseq zero is unknown, but zero participates in the same minimum-to-maximum chronology.
Ordinary source-system and site heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples.

claims.statement: Reports with rseq greater than the accession minimum are expected to be later report versions and generally addendums, but real-world exceptions and the relationship to the processing-derived imaging addendum_flag have not been directly validated.
caveats: A later report version may not constitute an addendum in the strict clinical sense; do not infer that one flag identifies a particular report revision.

claims.statement: Joining report rows to finding-grain tables by accession can multiply both report and finding rows.
caveats: Aggregate or select reports only under an explicit report policy.
Use minimum and maximum rseq for earliest and latest represented report versions; do not rely on tuple uniqueness.
Treat report text as potentially sensitive and do not expose raw values through this context service.

open-v2.risk-context.title: Open-v2 risk-assessment context
open-v2.risk-context.summary: Risk outputs were calculated during clinical care in MagView and ordinary values are tentatively believed to use percentage points, but the risk table, field variants, exceptional values, and model versions require internal investigation.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores named IBIS and NCI numeric outputs at risk-assessment grain with patient, accession, and study-date references.
caveats: A released name is not a complete clinical definition.

claims.statement: Ordinary NCI and IBIS outputs are tentatively believed to use percentage points, but the risk table has not been validated in depth. IBISPOP10, IBISPOPL, and IBIS_TD1 through IBIS_TD4 lack confirmed definitions; meanings of -35, -2, and 100 and the generating model versions are also unknown.
caveats: Treat percentage-point formatting as tentative and do not infer a comparable range from numeric physical type.

claims.statement: The risk-to-exam relationship is optional and does not establish that every exam has a risk record.
caveats: No empirical coverage measurement belongs in this catalog.

claims.statement: The released risk scores were calculated during clinical care and extracted from the breast-imaging MagView EHR system.
caveats: Clinical-time calculation does not by itself establish the exact calculation timestamp within the study episode.
Risk output and BI-RADS assessment are different constructs and must not be substituted for one another.
No field is approved for modeling or release merely because it appears in risk_anon.

open-v2.temporal-availability-context.title: Open-v2 temporal availability guardrail
open-v2.temporal-availability-context.summary: Open-v2 dates use a consistent per-patient random shift, preserving within-patient ordering and date differences while obscuring absolute calendar dates.

claims.statement: Open-v2 exposes exam, procedure, and pathology-report date fields in separate clinical surfaces.
caveats: Absolute calendar values are anonymized and must not be interpreted literally.

claims.statement: EMBED applies one consistent random date shift per patient across that patient's dates, so within-patient ordering and date differences are reliable while absolute day, month, and year are not.
caveats: Do not compare absolute calendar dates across patients.

claims.statement: Co-location of fields in combined_anon does not establish that they were observed at the same clinical time.
caveats: The wide table's construction remains unresolved.

claims.statement: Combined_anon projects patient, exam, finding, procedure, and pathology fields onto wide rows; those projections do not establish that repeated attributes are authoritative, that each clinical object has wide-row identity, or that fields were co-available.
caveats: Use canonical or co-located normalized bindings to understand object representation before relying on a wide projection.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 feature bindings contain exam, procedure, and pathology-report dates but no specimen-collection date or universal downstream-availability timestamp.
caveats: A missing binding does not prove that the clinical event or availability transition did not occur.
Task-specific cohort, follow-up, label, and modality-inclusion choices are analysis policies rather than dataset claims; agents must choose and defend them outside the portable catalog.
